chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The free person and the slave do not inherit (each other).
ai.seo_question: Do a free person and a slave inherit from each other in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the prominent chain of Shaykh al-Kulayni, establishes the legal principle of 'hijab al-dam' (barrier of blood/status) where differing degrees of freedom prevent mutual inheritance. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores that the ontological distinction between a free person (hurri) and a slave (mamluk) creates a structural impediment to wealth transfer, reflecting the social hierarchy of the time. It serves as a foundational text for understanding how status categories function as legal barriers in the distribution of estate shares.
